title: Brief executives and boards: the short story, the ask, the decision
summary: Senior people have little time. Lead with the point and the decision you need, then give only the detail that supports it.

beginner: Start with the bottom line: what you want and why, in one or two sentences.
State the decision or help you need.
Add three supporting points at most.
Practise saying it in under two minutes.
intermediate: Tailor the story to what each leader cares about.
Bring options with a recommendation, not just a problem.
Pre-brief key people before the meeting.
experienced: Brief boards on strategy, risk and results with the same structure.
Handle tough questions by going back to the bottom line.
Coach your PMs to brief leaders well.

toolExamples.google-docs: Write a one-page brief with the bottom line at the top.
toolExamples.claude: Ask an AI assistant to shorten your draft, then check it still says what you mean.

definitionOfDone: Brief leads with the bottom line
pitfalls: Building up to the point slowly
